title: BBC Learning English from the News 2026 — Quiz 3
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q021_shutter
elements.title: The repairs will force the owners to ___ the shop for two weeks.

elements.name: q022_snowflake
elements.title: As an insult, what does “snowflake” imply about the person being described?
choices: They are considered too easily offended.
elements.correctAnswer: They are considered too easily offended.

elements.name: q023_have_it_tough
elements.title: Students who juggle evening shifts and early classes often ___ during exam season.

elements.name: q024_forge
elements.title: After months of meetings, the two teams managed to ___ a strong partnership.

elements.name: q025_loom_large
elements.title: As the deadline approaches, funding problems ___ in the team's discussions.

elements.name: q026_time_is_on_someone_s_side
elements.title: “Nora can wait for a better offer. Time is on her side.” What does the second sentence mean?
choices: She is waiting for a deadline that has already passed.
She has plenty of time to decide.
She has already missed her chance.
elements.correctAnswer: She has plenty of time to decide.

elements.name: q027_hotline
elements.title: For urgent help, residents can ring a dedicated ___ that connects them directly to trained staff.

elements.name: q028_kill_switch
elements.title: Which term means a control that can stop equipment immediately in an emergency?

elements.name: q029_slowdown
elements.title: Orders are still rising, but less quickly than last year. The company reported a ___ in growth.

elements.name: q030_hoax
elements.title: The supposed sighting was a ___ staged with a model and a hidden camera.
